title: Cohomological Brown representability on the adic localizing hull
statement:
Fix a universe u, a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ in universe u of positive
characteristic different from $\ell$, a separated finite-type $k$-scheme X, and a
commutative condensed coefficient ring $\Lambda$ with the certificate of one of the
three adic families [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting; def-sfb-adic-coefficient-certificate].
Let $\mathcal L_X$ be the full localizing hull of the bounded constructible objects
inside the ordinary unbounded category $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{p_X^*\Lambda})$,
with ambient coproducts indexed in universe u+1
[def-sfb-bounded-constructible-localizing-closure]. For every additive-group-valued
cohomological functor $H:\mathcal L_X^{op}\to\mathrm{Ab}_{u+1}$ which sends
all these coproducts to products, the underlying set-valued functor of H is
representable by an object of $\mathcal L_X$.

proof.text: The source-library instance makes internal module objects Grothendieck abelian directly. Since X is finite type over a field and quasi-compact, it is a Noetherian scheme. The local-presentation embedding theorem gives an essentially small constructible heart.

Replace the heart predicate by its isomorphism closure and apply the bounded-homology Postnikov theorem. Bounded constructible complexes form a subclass of this essentially small class. Derived local smallness is supplied by the existing source instance.

The inclusion and minimality theorems of the intersection hull identify it with the localizing hull of the essentially small bounded constructible class. Apply the set-generated derived solution-set theorem to H.

The hull already has small coproducts and split idempotents. Apply the proved solution-set representability criterion: form a weak universal element, kill its kernel endomorphisms, show the resulting idempotent kills all kernel maps, split it, and obtain natural Hom bijections.

proof_origin.place: Formalized essential-smallness and solution-set representability; the set-generated derived solution-set construction remains a named intermediate theorem.
